mainEntity.name: What does the GI-MAP test measure?

acceptedAnswer.text: It uses DNA to quantify your gut bacteria, potential pathogens, parasites, yeast, H. pylori, and markers of inflammation and digestion, from a single at-home stool sample. That gives a precise picture of what is actually driving gut symptoms.

mainEntity.name: How is GI-MAP different from a regular stool test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Standard stool tests look for a few obvious problems. GI-MAP uses DNA to quantify a wide range of organisms and digestive markers at once, which is far more sensitive for the subtle imbalances behind chronic gut issues.

mainEntity.name: Do I collect the GI-MAP at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. After your consult you receive an at-home kit, collect a single stool sample, and send it to the lab. Dr. Nina reviews the results with you afterward and builds the plan.

It is worth it when gut symptoms are driving your health and the results will change your plan. Ordered for the right reason and interpreted by a clinician, it can save months of guesswork; run randomly with no one reading it, it is just a printout.

mainEntity.name: Can I order a GI-MAP without a doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Kits are sold online, but you are then left to interpret a dense report alone. Here it is ordered off your symptoms and read by a physician who turns it into an actual gut-repair plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I just do the test without becoming a patient?

acceptedAnswer.text: Testing here is always part of physician-led care. You start with a $99 Symptom Consultation so it is ordered for the right reason and the results are actually used.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: GI-MAP gut testing in Atlanta that finds the real reason behind the bloat and reflux.

paragraphs: If you have lived with the bloat, the reflux, and the irregularity while every basic test comes back fine, the problem was never imaginary. It is that nobody has actually looked at what is living in your gut.

I am Dr. Nina Ross, ND PhD. The GI-MAP maps your gut bacteria, pathogens, and digestion markers by DNA, and I read it as one move inside a plan that repairs what it finds. That is how a scary printout becomes a real path forward.

sections.label: What it is

headings.text: A DNA-level look at what is actually living in your gut.

paragraphs: The GI-MAP uses DNA to measure the bacteria, pathogens, parasites, yeast, and inflammation markers in your gut. That precision is real and genuinely useful, and it pays off when a clinician reads it against your symptoms and turns it into a repair plan.
It quantifies the good, the bad, and the opportunistic, so we are not guessing at what is off.
It flags parasites, H. pylori, and how well you are actually breaking food down and absorbing it.
Dr. Nina interprets it against your symptoms and history, so the results actually mean something.

sections.label: Who it's for

headings.text: The GI-MAP is right for some people. It is wrong for others.

eyebrowSpans: It is not for you if
paragraphs: If that second list stung a little, good. That honesty is exactly what you are paying for here.

boldPairs.body: You have ongoing bloat, reflux, irregularity, or food reactions with no clear cause
You suspect a gut driver behind fatigue, skin, mood, or autoimmune issues
You want a clinician to turn the results into a real gut-repair plan

boldPairs.title: It is not for you if

boldPairs.body: You want raw numbers with no interest in what to do about them
You are hoping a test alone will fix a gut a test can only measure
You expect one panel to replace an ongoing relationship with a clinician

sections.label: Not a mail-order kit

headings.text: Anyone can sell you a gut kit now. Reading it is the hard part.

paragraphs: Order a kit online and you get a tube, a dense printout, and a forum to panic in. No one connecting the findings to your symptoms, no plan when the results land. Here, the GI-MAP is ordered for a reason and interpreted by a physician, as one tool inside a plan that repairs what it finds.
